messages:
Morgan: Heads up — noticed a 2x tail latency spike for multi-tenant infer calls out of eu-west-rack-12 starting ~08:12 UTC. p99 went from 85ms -> 420ms.
infra-bot: alert: euw-rack-12 egress-saturation detected (NIC drops 18%, queue depth 95%). Incident ID: I-2026-0320-231
Alex: on it, can you paste `tc -s qdisc` and `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` from a few affected nodes?
Morgan: pasted output below:
```
# tc -s qdisc
qdisc fq_codel 0: dev eth0 root refcnt 2 limit 1000p
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
  drop 0 pkts
# netstat -s | grep -i drop
            184k packets dropped
# nvidia-smi pmon -c 1
GPU  PID  Type  Sm  Mem  Enc  Dec  Command
0    0    C     30  40   0    0    tenant-worker
```
Not great — NIC tx drops and kernel tx queue swell.
Priya: KV cache miss-rate for the same tenant cohort jumped from 6% -> 38% around the same time (correlates). Sounds like cross-tenant egress or PCIe saturation causing queueing and KV eviction thrash.
Sam: if this is rack-level oversubscribe on the top-of-rack trunk, we should consider two short-term moves: 1) soft-evict noisy tenants off the rack to reserved (dedicated) slices, or 2) apply the fairbackoff queuing tweak we've been testing. Both have tradeoffs (cost vs cache warmup).
Dani: agree. Running a mass migration will cold-start KV caches and may spike token costs. What's the expected perf delta if we flip fairbackoff? Alex: from the lab run, fairbackoff drops p99 by ~35% under 1.3x load and keeps mean roughly flat. It buys headroom without moving tenants.
Morgan: can we try fairbackoff on euw-rack-12 as a canary at 10% of traffic? Need a rollback plan if KV thrash gets worse.
Alex: plan: push ff flag `scheduler.fairbackoff.v2` to rack-12 via `rollout --rack euw-rack-12 --canary 10%` and monitor kv_hit_rate, p50/p95/p99, and NIC drops. If kv_hit_rate drops >10pp or p99 increases, rollback.
Priya: note: if we route tenants off-rack to dedicated slices, request-level sequencer pins may break — need to ensure prefix K/V pinning migrates. That requires 5m of coordination between routing and cache owners.
Sam: finance note — temporary dedicated slices cost ~3x the transient unit cost. If we migrate 25% of traffic for 4 hours, expect +$2.4k for that window (ballpark). Is that acceptable for an on-call mitigation?
Dani: ops decision: try fairbackoff canary first, then if no improvement after 12m escalate to targeted migrations for top-3 noisy tenants. I'll own the canary rollout at 20:00 UTC.
infra-bot: scheduled rollout: scheduler.fairbackoff.v2 -> euw-rack-12 (canary 10%) at 20:00 UTC. Auto-monitoring hooks: KV.hit_rate, NIC.drops, tail_latency.p99. Auto-rollback: true.
Morgan: thanks. Also please add a quick dashboard card for "rack trunk egress utilization" and set alert at 80% to catch this earlier.
Alex: will add dashboard and a lightweight probe that hits representative route at 10s interval.
Priya: postmortem notes: follow-up items: 1) look into preemptive KV warming on migration, 2) validate our routing handshake ensures seq pinning, 3) long-term: propose rack-shielding — reserve 2 NIC lanes per rack for high-SLA tenants.
Sam: +1 on rack-shielding; can model cost and capacity tradeoffs tomorrow.
Dani: logging the action items in #incidents and will update after the canary.
Morgan: cb — if the canary fails I'll open an urgent migration plan. Thanks team :)
